Current alignment targets approval, preference, reward, compliance—and a verdict can satisfy all of these while nothing can show it mistaken: then it can be altered or replaced, never corrected. Only one structure makes verdicts correctable and correction cumulative: a shared, endorsement-independent standard fixes the correctness question, and vindication proceeds only through grounds that can be cited, contested, and redeployed as bearing on that standard. Where the grounds bearing on a standing are held fixed, no difference in that standing can be vindicated.
